_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Contracts CI forge-test matrix.
`.github/workflows/contracts-ci.yml` builds its matrix from this file via
`scripts/check-test-slice-coverage.mjs --emit-matrix`, and the SAME script
asserts that every contracts/test/**/*.t.sol is claimed by exactly one slice
or by an explicit `excluded` entry. Keeping the patterns here (rather than
inline in the workflow) is deliberate: a guard that carries its own private
copy of the pattern list can pass while the matrix runs nothing.
`pattern` is a GLOB, not a regex — it is passed verbatim to
`forge test --match-path`. Two rules bite constantly:
* A PREFIX pattern cannot reach a subdirectory. `test/Audit*.t.sol` does
NOT match `test/v4/Audit20260712_POLIsolation.t.sol`, because after
`test/` the path continues `v4/`, not `Audit`. This is what left 13
files unrun for weeks. Note the reason is the PREFIX, not the star:
forge does not set globset's `literal_separator`, so `*` DOES cross
`/` — `test/*Invariants.t.sol` matches all 7 files under
`test/invariants/` (verified against forge 1.5.1). Write an explicit
`test/<dir>/*.t.sol` slice for each subdirectory. A brace CAN span
sibling directories — `test/{base,markets,nftfi,v2,vaults}/*.t.sol`
matches all five (verified against forge 1.5.1) — so a handful of
small subdirectories can share ONE slice rather than spawning a CI
job each. Prefer widening that brace to adding a slice: a matrix job
costs a recursive submodule checkout, a Foundry install and a compile
before it runs its first test, and total wall-clock is max(slice),
not sum(slice). `test/nftfi/` (3 files, 51 tests) was folded in on
2026-08-21 for exactly that reason: it takes the slice from 143 to
194 runnable tests, still a quarter of the largest slice
(`audit-early`, 765), so it moves the critical path not at all,
whereas a 12th job would pay the full per-job overhead for 51 fast
unit tests. Fold until a slice approaches the largest one; split
only when folding would make it the new longest job.
NOTE `test/nftfi/NftfiMocks.sol` is a shared harness, not a test, and
needs NO slice and NO excluded[] entry: exclusions are matched only
against `*.t.sol`, so an entry naming it would match zero files and
trip the stale-exclusion check. The stray-file guard already covers
it — it fails if a non-`.t.sol` under test/ declares test*/invariant_*.
ADDING A SUBDIRECTORY UNDER test/ WITHOUT TOUCHING THIS FILE IS THE
RECURRING FAILURE: the guard catches it, but only after the fact.
* regex syntax (`|`, `$`, `\.`) is matched LITERALLY and silently finds
nothing, because forge exits 0 on 'No tests found in project!'.
`noMatchTest` is the shared `--no-match-test` regex applied to every slice.
It filters by TEST NAME. It is ANCHORED (`^`) on purpose: it was once the
substring `(Invariant|invariant|Fuzz|fuzz|testFuzz)`, which skipped 15
deterministic unit tests purely because of how they were SPELLED — among
them test_ATTACK4_kInvariantDecrease (a red-team test), four AMM k-invariant
swap/mint-burn guards and three R018 staking-shortfall pins. All 15 pass;
they simply never ran. Every genuine fuzz/invariant uses the `testFuzz_` /
`invariant_` PREFIX, so anchoring skips exactly those and nothing else.
Keep it anchored — an unanchored edit silently re-hides tests by name.
A slice MAY override it with its own `noMatchTest` — the `invariants` slice
does, because the shared default would strip every test it exists to run.
The override is not a loophole: the per-slice guard asserts the slice still
yields >=1 runnable test UNDER ITS EFFECTIVE FILTER, so an override that
silences everything fails loudly instead of passing over nothing.

excluded.reason: Echidna property definitions (`echidna_*`). forge's collector only picks up `test*` / `invariant_*`, so `forge test` finds zero runnable tests in this directory no matter what pattern points at it. Requires the `echidna` binary, which is not installed in this workflow.
Halmos symbolic specs (`check_*`). Same story as echidna: forge collects zero tests from these files. Requires the `halmos` binary, which is not installed in this workflow.
